newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH RAIL DEAL OPENS WAY FOR ADTRANZ INVESTMENT.
newsitem.headline: POLISH RAIL DEAL OPENS WAY FOR ADTRANZ INVESTMENT.

text.p: The Polish State Railways (PKP) have clinched an initial deal with the rolling stock maker Pafawag SA on buying from it 50 locomotives, in a move likely to trigger the latter firm's sale to Adtranz .

PKP said in a statement on Thursday that under the deal, to be followed by more talks before a final agreement is signed, first high-speed electric state-of-the-art locomotives will be delivered in 1997.

The agreement is likely to be followed by the sale of Pafawag to Adtranz, a joint venture of ABB group and Daimler-Benz AG, which has declared it will buy the Polish company if it wins the PKP contract.

In a tentative agreement with the government, signed in September, Adtranz said it would pay $3.7 million for a 75 percent stake in the ailing Pafawag, bring modern technology there and invest $28.1 million over the next six years.
The agreement is to become effective when Pafawag, based in the south-western city of Wroclaw, and PKP agree on a locomotive delivery programme.

Adtranz would then increase Pafawag's capital by $6 million and launch the production of a high-speed state-of-the-art locomotive. Pafawag's employment is to be maintained at the current level of 1,620 people.
An Adtranz official said on Thursday the company would issue a statement later in the day.
